title: The test crashes right after checking for nullptr
summary: A failed EXPECT_NE lets the test carry on to the next line. Checks that later lines depend on belong in ASSERT_, and an ASSERT_ inside a helper is caught with ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE.

turns.user: changed parse_config and now the test binary dies with Segmentation fault. i see the ReadsPort failure and then nothing. i literally check nullptr with EXPECT_NE??

assistant.body: Great question! EXPECT_ macros only record a failure. The test function keeps going to the next line. So after EXPECT_NE(config, nullptr) fails, config->port still runs, dereferences nullptr, and takes the whole process down with it. Any check that later lines depend on should be an ASSERT_. It returns from the test function on failure, so the remaining tests still run and get reported. ReadsHosts checks neither nullptr nor the size before hosts[0], so it gets both.

turns.user: ok. moved the parse + null check into a helper since i write it everywhere, now ASSERT_NE doesnt compile. GoogleTest_NotSupported_OnFunctionReturningNonVoid ???

assistant.body: Note: on failure an ASSERT_ expands to a plain return with no value, so it only works in a function that returns void. The helper hands its result back through a pointer instead. One more thing worth knowing: that ASSERT_ only leaves the helper. The test that called it carries on. Wrap the call in ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE and the test stops as soon as the helper hits a fatal failure.
